7951.content:
Mobile camera permission is the user's runtime authorization for an application to access device camera hardware. The platform project must declare the required capability and handle the result of the user's permission decision.

The emotion detector cannot perform its central feature without a camera, but the book notes that other applications should consider degraded behavior when permission is refused. Permission is therefore both a platform configuration and a product-design boundary.

7954.title: ML.NET
7954.heading: ML.NET
7954.content:
ML.NET is a machine-learning framework for building and consuming models from .NET applications. It provides data-loading, transformation, training, evaluation, and prediction APIs that integrate with C# types and ordinary application projects.

The framework organizes work as a pipeline rather than hiding the decisions required for useful learning. A successful application still depends on representative data, an algorithm suited to the task, appropriate metrics, and validation against data not used for training.

7957.heading: ML.NET Data View
7957.content:
`IDataView` is ML.NET's tabular data abstraction for columns with defined names and types. It supports lazy, cursor-based access so pipelines can work with datasets that need not be fully loaded into memory.

Loaders create data views from files or in-memory objects, and transformations produce new logical views without immediately materializing every value. The schema connects application data to pipeline stages and must match the columns an estimator expects.

7960.heading: ML.NET Learning Pipeline
7960.content:
An ML.NET learning pipeline chains estimators that prepare columns and train an algorithm. Fitting the pipeline against training data produces a transformer capable of applying the learned sequence to compatible input data.

Keeping preparation and learning in one pipeline ensures the same transformations are applied during training and prediction. The fitted pipeline can be saved as a model artifact together with the input schema required to load it later.

7963.content:
ML.NET data preparation converts raw columns into values an algorithm can learn from. Common steps include replacing missing values, mapping categorical values to keys, normalizing numeric inputs, and combining selected columns into a feature vector.

Preparation choices become part of the model's semantics, not merely cleanup. They must be fitted on training data and replayed consistently for evaluation and production predictions to avoid leakage or incompatible inputs.

7966.title: Mixture Likelihood
7966.heading: Mixture Likelihood
7966.content:
Mixture likelihood evaluates each observation under the weighted sum of all component densities and multiplies those values across the data set. Membership is latent and integrated through the sum.

Maximizing this likelihood estimates parameters for overlapping components. It provides a basis for comparing fitted model structures when complexity is also controlled.

7969.title: Mixture Distribution Clustering
7969.heading: Mixture Distribution Clustering
7969.content:
Mixture distribution clustering represents the population density as a weighted sum of component densities. Each component corresponds to a latent group and contributes according to its mixture weight.

Learning estimates the component parameters and the probability that each observation arose from each group. Gaussian components are common for numerical data.

7972.title: Mixture Component
7972.heading: Mixture Component
7972.content:
A mixture component is one probability distribution available under a particular value of a mixture model's hidden choice variable. Each component can represent a distinct behavior, class, process, or local approximation.

The mixture combines components without requiring the observation to be assigned to one with certainty. Component weights express how often or under which inputs each model contributes, while posterior inference can update those weights from evidence.

7974.title: Mixture Component Weight

7975.sourceSearchName: mixture component weight mixture component weight
7975.title: Mixture Component Weight
7975.heading: Mixture Component Weight
7975.content:
A mixture component weight is the prior probability that an observation comes from a particular component. All component weights are positive and sum to one.

The weight represents expected cluster prevalence before the observation's attributes are considered. Together with the component density, it determines the posterior membership probability.

7981.content:
Mixed-initiative dialog allows both the user and assistant to steer the interaction. The assistant can ask for needed information, while the user can volunteer values, correct assumptions, change goals, or request help.

It combines the task control of [[Directed Dialog]] with the flexibility of [[Open Dialog]]. The [[Dialog Manager]] must accept relevant information even when it arrives outside the anticipated order.

7984.title: Mixed Reality
7984.heading: Mixed Reality
7984.content:
Mixed reality is a set of approaches in which real and virtual information are combined in different proportions. It includes both [[Virtual Reality]] and [[Augmented Reality]].

A system can be located on a continuum whose extremes are a purely real environment and a purely virtual one. Its position on that continuum may change as the user interacts. The concept is useful because interfaces can share components and problems even when they mix physical and synthetic content differently.

Near the real end, [[Augmented Reality]] makes the physical world the primary place of action and adds registered virtual information. Near the virtual end, augmented virtuality brings selected real-world imagery or participants into a primarily synthetic environment. The continuum classifies the resulting experience rather than requiring one display technology.

7987.title: Missingness Indicator
7987.heading: Missingness Indicator
7987.content:
A missingness indicator is a binary variable that marks whether another variable is absent or contains a code treated as unknown. It makes the distribution of missing information explicit and supports checks against the original field.

The indicator can help audit exclusions or describe a missing category, but it does not restore the missing measurement. If most outcome-positive records lack a required time value, a flag exposes a severe data limitation that imputation may not credibly solve.

The book also reviews missingness at the variable level before modeling. Fields that are entirely or largely missing may be excluded or handled explicitly, while rough imputation is reserved for exploratory workflows whose limitations are understood.

7990.title: Misinformation
7990.heading: Misinformation
7990.content:
Misinformation is false or inaccurate information that misleads people and may be spread without an intention to deceive. Open social platforms allow it to propagate rapidly through ordinary sharing and trust relationships.

It is distinguished from deliberate [[Disinformation]], although real cascades may mix both intentions. Analysis can target the content, the accounts spreading it, its diffusion structure, or interventions that limit its effects.

Misinformation spreader detection identifies accounts responsible for generating or amplifying deceptive content. It combines profile, behavior, sentiment, content, and social-link features to distinguish malicious users from ordinary participants.

Detecting the account can expose many messages at once, but supervised methods require credible labels. Suspension lists, manual annotation, and [[Social Honeypot|social honeypots]] each introduce different delays and sampling biases.

7999.title: Misinformation Diffusion
7999.heading: Misinformation Diffusion
7999.content:
Misinformation diffusion is the network process through which inaccurate claims move from senders to spreaders and receivers. Exposure affects belief and trust but does not guarantee that every contacted person adopts the claim.

Network connectivity, local leaders, communities, and forceful individuals alter the eventual consensus. This makes belief-exchange models a useful complement to epidemic-style information-spreading models.

8002.title: Misinformation Detection
8002.heading: Misinformation Detection
8002.content:
Misinformation detection estimates whether a social message or claim is inaccurate. A learning system derives a compact representation from raw content, trains against identity labels, and updates its estimator to reduce classification loss.

Evidence may come from language, sentiment, timing, users, or diffusion structure. Reliable evaluation depends on labels whose collection process and class imbalance are made explicit.

8005.title: Mirai Botnet
8005.heading: Mirai Botnet
8005.content:
The Mirai botnet infected Internet-connected devices by exploiting weak or default credentials and coordinated them for large denial-of-service attacks. Its scale came from many ordinary embedded devices that were reachable, poorly administered, and easy to compromise automatically.

Mirai connects [[Internet of Things Security]] to broader network consequences: a device with little local value can still supply attack capacity as a [[Zombie Computer]] in a [[Botnet]].

8008.content:
A mipmap chain stores progressively smaller, prefiltered versions of a texture, commonly halving each dimension at every level. A renderer selects an appropriate level as the textured object becomes smaller on screen.

This avoids repeatedly sampling a full-resolution image for a surface that covers only a few pixels. Mipmaps reduce aliasing and can improve cache use, but UV islands need adequate padding so lower-resolution filtering does not bleed unrelated colors across their boundaries.

A minimum-norm solution is the solution of an underdetermined system with the smallest Euclidean length. It removes ambiguity among infinitely many exact solutions by choosing the one closest to the origin.

This vector is orthogonal to the null space and lies in the row space of the coefficient matrix. A [[Pseudoinverse]] computes it directly.

A minimum support threshold is the smallest transaction fraction an itemset must reach to be treated as frequent. It controls how aggressively association-rule mining prunes rare combinations.

A high threshold can miss important uncommon patterns, while a low one can produce an overwhelming candidate set. The choice should reflect the application and database size.

Minimum redundancy maximum relevance selects features that are strongly related to the target while avoiding variables that repeat information already supplied by selected features. It balances usefulness against overlap rather than scoring each variable in isolation.

The mRMR search can be redesigned for parallel platforms because relevance and redundancy calculations become expensive across many features and records. Parallelism must preserve the criterion while dividing its calculations.

8038.content:
The minimum content of natural law describes basic constraints that any durable legal order must address because people are vulnerable, resources are limited, and cooperation is necessary. It does not collapse law into morality, but recognizes practical conditions that law cannot ignore.

The argument opens a place for intrinsic limits within legal positivism. Privacy may be connected to those conditions when some protected independence is necessary for agency and social life.

8041.title: Minimization Problem
8041.heading: Minimization Problem
8041.content:
A minimization problem asks for the permitted solution that gives an objective function its smallest value. The function converts the quality of a candidate into a quantity that can be compared with other candidates.

Neural-network training treats prediction error as a [[Loss Function]] and changes weights and biases to reduce it. The network does not need to know the minimum in advance; local derivative information indicates changes that make the current loss smaller.

A minimization may be unconstrained or limited to [[Feasible Solution|feasible solutions]] by equations and inequalities. A [[Local Minimum]] is best only in a neighborhood, while the global solution is best over the entire feasible set; convexity can make those notions coincide.

8044.title: Minimax
8044.heading: Minimax
8044.content:
Minimax selects a move under the assumption that the current player maximizes the evaluated outcome while the opponent minimizes it. Values are propagated upward through alternating maximum and minimum layers of a [[Game Tree]].

The algorithm is exact only when it reaches terminal states and their values are accurate. Depth-limited search substitutes a [[Static Evaluation Function]], and [[Alpha-Beta Pruning]] avoids branches that cannot affect the final choice.

Every submodule that has a primary decomposition also has a minimal one. The minimal associated primes are intrinsic, while components belonging to [[Embedded Prime]]s can show more dependence on the chosen decomposition.

8050.title: Minimal Polynomial
8050.heading: Minimal Polynomial
8050.content:
The minimal polynomial of an algebraic element c over K is the unique monic irreducible polynomial in K[x] having c as a root. Every polynomial over K that vanishes at c is divisible by it.

Its degree equals the degree of the simple extension K(c) over K.

8053.title: Minimal Free Resolution
8053.heading: Minimal Free Resolution
8053.content:
A minimal free resolution uses the smallest possible number of generators at every stage. Over a Noetherian local or graded local ring, its differentials have entries in the relevant maximal ideal.

Minimal resolutions are unique up to isomorphism under the source's hypotheses. Their free ranks and degree shifts give [[Graded Betti Number]]s, projective dimension, and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity.

8056.title: Minicomputer
8056.heading: Minicomputer
8056.content:
A minicomputer was a smaller, less expensive computer designed for direct use in laboratories, departments, and industrial systems. It occupied the space between centralized mainframes and later microprocessor-based personal computers.

Companies such as DEC built minicomputers around transistor and integrated-circuit technology. Their interactive use and customer-developed applications prepared users for personal computing.

8059.title: Mind Projection Fallacy
8059.heading: Mind Projection Fallacy
8059.content:
The mind projection fallacy occurs when uncertainty in a modeler's knowledge is projected onto the external phenomenon as though the uncertainty were a property of the thing itself. A probability assignment then appears to describe inherent randomness rather than a conditional state of information.

Keeping preliminary knowledge explicit avoids this confusion. The distribution states what can be inferred under a description, while the phenomenon may contain unmodeled structure that different evidence could reveal.

8062.title: Middleware
8062.heading: Middleware
8062.content:
Middleware is software that connects applications, data, and lower-level computing facilities. It sits between operating systems and business applications and supplies common communication, integration, database, messaging, or management capabilities.

The book groups middleware as message-oriented, data-oriented, or object-oriented according to what participants share. In a cloud platform, middleware forms part of the operating environment supplied above the raw infrastructure.

8064.sourceSearchName: microsoft bot framework microsoft bot framework
8064.title: Microsoft Bot Framework
8064.heading: Document

8065.sourceSearchName: microsoft bot framework microsoft bot framework
8065.title: Microsoft Bot Framework
8065.heading: Microsoft Bot Framework
8065.content:
Microsoft Bot Framework is the service and programming framework used to receive conversational activities, run bot logic, and send replies through supported channels. It hides much of the state-machine and transport plumbing while leaving response behavior to the application.

The 2019 project begins with an echo-bot template, processes message activities through an adapter, adds LUIS-based intent recognition, and deploys the bot to Azure App Service. A separate channel registration then connects clients to the published messaging endpoint.

8066.title: Microsoft Bot Framework

8067.title: Microsoft BASIC for Altair

8068.sourceSearchName: microsoft basic for altair microsoft basic for altair
8068.title: Microsoft BASIC for Altair
8068.heading: Microsoft BASIC for Altair
8068.content:
Bill Gates and Paul Allen created a BASIC interpreter for the Altair using a DEC PDP-10 as their development system. The program let owners write software in a simple high-level language instead of entering machine instructions.

It was Microsoft’s first product and demonstrated that software would determine the personal computer’s usefulness. The same language moved from a shared mainframe setting to a machine owned by one person.

8071.title: Microsoft Azure
8071.heading: Microsoft Azure
8071.content:
Microsoft Azure is the cloud platform used in the book to host the React client, ASP.NET Core API, and SQL database. These parts are created as related resources and configured with their deployed URLs and environment-specific values.

The platform changes where the system runs, not the contracts among its parts. Routing, cross-origin access, authentication settings, database connectivity, and build artifacts must all match the hosted environment.

8074.title: Microservice
8074.heading: Microservice
8074.content:
A microservice is a small, independently operated process responsible for a bounded capability. The order-processing example treats autonomy as the defining property: the worker can continue running even when no new orders arrive and does not require another application process to remain alive.

Independent deployment and scaling can isolate change, but dividing one system into many services adds network, versioning, logging, and data-consistency problems. The book cautions that a microservice architecture is useful only when those costs solve a real need.

The design-patterns source frames a microservice as a small unit built around one business capability, loosely coupled by an explicit service contract, independently maintainable, and responsible for isolated state. Those boundaries permit different services and their data stores to scale or deploy at different rates, rather than merely splitting a monolith into smaller processes that still share one database.

8076.sourceSearchName: microscopic meaning of temperature microscopic meaning of temperature
8076.title: Microscopic Meaning of Temperature
8076.heading: Document

8077.sourceSearchName: microscopic meaning of temperature microscopic meaning of temperature
8077.title: Microscopic Meaning of Temperature
8077.heading: Microscopic Meaning of Temperature
8077.content:
Temperature represents the energetic activity of a material's elementary particles. Adding internal energy increases translational, rotational, and vibrational motion, while removing energy reduces those modes of molecular activity.

The material state changes how that activity transports energy. Closely packed particles favor [[Fourier Heat Conduction Law|conduction]], mobile fluid particles add bulk transport, and electromagnetic radiation can carry energy without an intervening material medium.

8078.sourceSearchName: microscopic meaning of temperature microscopic meaning of temperature
8078.title: Microscopic Meaning of Temperature
8078.heading: References

8079.sourceSearchName: microprocessor support chip ecosystem microprocessor support chip ecosystem
8079.title: Microprocessor Support Chip Ecosystem
8079.heading: Document

8080.sourceSearchName: microprocessor support chip ecosystem microprocessor support chip ecosystem
8080.title: Microprocessor Support Chip Ecosystem
8080.heading: Microprocessor Support Chip Ecosystem
8080.content:
A microprocessor becomes a usable computer when paired with memory, input-output controllers, clocks, and other support circuits. Offering a compatible family of chips lets customers configure one processor for many products.

Intel used this ecosystem to answer the commonality problem. Standard building blocks reduced custom hardware work while preserving application-specific behavior in software and peripheral choices.

8081.sourceSearchName: microprocessor support chip ecosystem microprocessor support chip ecosystem
8081.title: Microprocessor Support Chip Ecosystem
8081.heading: References

8082.sourceSearchName: microprocessor commonality problem microprocessor commonality problem
8082.title: Microprocessor Commonality Problem
8082.heading: Document

8083.sourceSearchName: microprocessor commonality problem microprocessor commonality problem
8083.title: Microprocessor Commonality Problem
8083.heading: Microprocessor Commonality Problem
8083.content:
As integrated circuits grew more complex, each custom logic design served a narrower market. The commonality problem asked how a dense chip could justify mass production when few customers needed exactly the same fixed function.

The microprocessor solved the dilemma by putting a programmable general-purpose processor on the chip. Memory, input-output, and software let many customers adapt the same device to different applications.

8084.sourceSearchName: microprocessor commonality problem microprocessor commonality problem
8084.title: Microprocessor Commonality Problem
8084.heading: References

8086.title: Microplanner
8086.heading: Microplanner
8086.content:
A microplanner turns a response plan into detailed linguistic decisions. It can choose sentence structure, referring expressions, aggregation, and the level of explicitness appropriate to the context.

Its output guides [[Lexicalization]], which realizes the structure as words and inflected forms. Together these stages separate what the assistant should say from exactly how it says it.

8089.title: Microphysiological System
8089.heading: Microphysiological System
8089.content:
A microphysiological system is an engineered in-vitro platform that reproduces selected physical and biological functions of human tissue at small scale. It often combines living cells, three-dimensional matrices, microfluidic flow, sensing, and controlled stimulation.

Its validity is specific to the modeled mechanism; no small platform should be assumed to represent every response of the source organ.

8092.title: Microfluidic Device
8092.heading: Microfluidic Device
8092.content:
A microfluidic device manipulates microliter-scale or smaller fluid volumes through networks of microscopic channels, valves, mixers, and pumps. Precisely controlled flow can deliver different media, cells, chemicals, and mechanical stimuli to separate regions.

The small scale suits tissue models and screening, although it does not directly solve fabrication of large replacement tissues.

8094.sourceSearchName: microcode for early microprocessors microcode for early microprocessors
8094.title: Microcode for Early Microprocessors
8094.heading: Document

8095.sourceSearchName: microcode for early microprocessors microcode for early microprocessors
8095.title: Microcode for Early Microprocessors
8095.heading: Microcode for Early Microprocessors
8095.content:
Microcode is a detailed program that coordinates the internal operations used to realize a processor’s instruction set. Early microprocessor systems stored these low-level routines in read-only or random-access memory.

A simple processor could therefore provide useful behavior through carefully designed control programs. The balance between hardware and microcode helped make a computer architecture just barely realizable on an early chip.

8096.sourceSearchName: microcode for early microprocessors microcode for early microprocessors
8096.title: Microcode for Early Microprocessors
8096.heading: References

8098.title: Microblog Clustering
8098.heading: Microblog Clustering
8098.content:
Microblog clustering groups brief, rapidly arriving posts using textual, temporal, social, and sometimes location signals. Individual messages are sparse and informal, while the underlying events and topics may change quickly.

Aggregating related terms or users can strengthen weak content evidence, and fading weights can track emerging conversations. Spam, repeated messages, and popular background topics must be controlled so they do not dominate the clusters.

8100.sourceSearchName: microarray data clustering microarray data clustering
8100.title: Microarray Data Clustering
8100.heading: Document

8101.sourceSearchName: microarray data clustering microarray data clustering
8101.title: Microarray Data Clustering
8101.heading: Microarray Data Clustering
8101.content:
Microarray clustering organizes genes or samples from large matrices of expression measurements. Gene clusters may reveal coordinated response across conditions, while sample clusters may suggest biological subtypes.

Measurements are noisy, dimensions greatly outnumber samples, and preprocessing choices can dominate proximity. Biological interpretation therefore combines statistical stability with functional or experimental evidence rather than treating clusters as definitive pathways.

8102.sourceSearchName: microarray data clustering microarray data clustering
8102.title: Microarray Data Clustering
8102.heading: References

8104.title: Micro ORM
8104.heading: Micro ORM
8104.content:
A micro ORM provides a small layer between application objects and relational query results. It commonly handles parameter binding and row-to-object mapping while leaving SQL creation and relational behavior explicit.

Dapper follows this model: it reduces low-level ADO.NET ceremony without becoming the owner of the database model. The tradeoff is that the application must deliberately design and maintain its SQL.

8106.sourceSearchName: mhd topping cycle mhd topping cycle
8106.title: MHD Topping Cycle
8106.heading: Document

8107.sourceSearchName: mhd topping cycle mhd topping cycle
8107.title: MHD Topping Cycle
8107.heading: MHD Topping Cycle
8107.content: An MHD topping cycle extracts electrical power while combustion gas is still very hot and conducting, then sends its remaining heat to a steam or gas-turbine bottoming plant. Conductivity drops as gas cools, so extending the MHD channel alone cannot use all of its thermal energy. Combining stages uses a wider temperature range and raises total fuel utilization over either stage alone.

8108.title: MHD Topping Cycle

8109.heading: Document

8110.sourceSearchName: mhd magnetic flux density mhd magnetic flux density
8110.title: MHD Magnetic Flux Density
8110.heading: MHD Magnetic Flux Density
8110.content: Magnetic flux density measures the field strength across the conducting flow of a [[Magnetohydrodynamic Generator]]. A stronger field raises induced voltage and potential electrical output, but conventional windings consume power and require cooling. The source discusses superconducting windings as a way to cut magnet resistance losses at the cost of cryogenic equipment. Field strength is therefore both a performance and plant-design decision.

8111.title: MHD Magnetic Flux Density

8112.title: MHD Generator Duct
8112.heading: Document

8113.sourceSearchName: mhd generator duct mhd generator duct
8113.title: MHD Generator Duct
8113.heading: MHD Generator Duct
8113.content: The generator duct guides fast ionized gas through the field and holds electrodes where current can be taken off. Its walls must tolerate heat, corrosion, electrical isolation, and erosion from seeded plasma. The source contrasts insulating ceramics with water-cooled metal segments separated by ceramic material. A long-lived smooth duct matters because wall damage and pressure drop reduce useful conversion.

8114.sourceSearchName: mhd generator duct mhd generator duct
8114.title: MHD Generator Duct
8114.heading: References

8115.sourceSearchName: mhd gas seeding mhd gas seeding
8115.title: MHD Gas Seeding
8115.heading: Document

8116.sourceSearchName: mhd gas seeding mhd gas seeding
8116.title: MHD Gas Seeding
8116.heading: MHD Gas Seeding
8116.content: Gas seeding introduces easily ionized material into the hot working gas of a [[Magnetohydrodynamic Generator]]. Cesium or potassium can supply charge carriers at temperatures lower than a pure gas would need for comparable conductivity. The improved electrical path raises possible output but creates costs and corrosion problems; an open-cycle plant also needs a way to recover and reuse its seed material.

8117.sourceSearchName: mhd gas seeding mhd gas seeding
8117.title: MHD Gas Seeding
8117.heading: References

8118.title: MHD Gas Electrical Conductivity
8118.heading: Document

8119.sourceSearchName: mhd gas electrical conductivity mhd gas electrical conductivity
8119.title: MHD Gas Electrical Conductivity
8119.heading: MHD Gas Electrical Conductivity
8119.content: Electrical conductivity lets a hot gas carry induced current between the electrodes of an [[Magnetohydrodynamic Generator]]. Pure gas requires extreme temperature for useful ionization; even a small ionized fraction can help, and [[MHD Gas Seeding]] raises it at less severe conditions. As gas cools through the channel, electrons and ions recombine, limiting further output and making downstream heat recovery valuable.

8120.title: MHD Gas Electrical Conductivity

8122.title: Metropolis Algorithm
8122.heading: Metropolis Algorithm
8122.content:
The Metropolis algorithm proposes a new state from the current one and accepts or rejects it using a ratio that preserves the desired target distribution. Rejections repeat the current state in the resulting Markov chain.

After a burn-in period, samples can approximate the target even when it is known only up to a normalization constant. Proposal size controls the tradeoff between frequent acceptance and effective movement through the state space.

8124.sourceSearchName: method of exhaustion method of exhaustion
8124.title: Method of Exhaustion
8124.heading: Document

8125.sourceSearchName: method of exhaustion method of exhaustion
8125.title: Method of Exhaustion
8125.heading: Method of Exhaustion
8125.content: The method of exhaustion approximates a geometric quantity with a sequence of inscribed or circumscribed figures whose error becomes arbitrarily small. Classical calculations of a disk's area use polygons with increasing numbers of sides. The method anticipates the modern idea of a [[Limit of a Sequence]] without requiring a closed-form value at each finite stage.

8126.sourceSearchName: method of exhaustion method of exhaustion
8126.title: Method of Exhaustion
8126.heading: References

8127.sourceSearchName: method of difference method of difference
8127.title: Method of Difference
8127.heading: Document

8128.sourceSearchName: method of difference method of difference
8128.title: Method of Difference
8128.heading: Method of Difference
8128.content:
The method of difference compares situations that vary in a candidate cause while other relevant circumstances are held as similar as possible. If the effect changes with that factor, the contrast supports a causal claim.

Real cases rarely differ in only one respect, and causes can depend on combinations of conditions. The method therefore motivates more rigorous [[Variational Induction]] rather than functioning as an infallible rule.

8129.sourceSearchName: method of difference method of difference
8129.title: Method of Difference
8129.heading: References

8130.heading: Document

8131.title: METAR and SPECI Reports
8131.heading: METAR and SPECI Reports
8131.content: A METAR is a standardized routine aerodrome weather observation, commonly issued hourly. A SPECI is an unscheduled special report produced when specified significant changes occur between routine observations. Both describe current conditions rather than the future conditions addressed by [[Terminal Aerodrome Forecasts]].

8134.title: Metal Hydride Hydrogen Storage
8134.heading: Metal Hydride Hydrogen Storage
8134.content: Some metals and alloys chemically bind hydrogen as solid hydrides. Heating the material later releases hydrogen for use, letting fuel be stored or transported in solid form. The source lists several candidate compounds but notes the heavy mass of hydride relative to recovered hydrogen. Bond strength, release heat, and material weight therefore matter beside storage safety and volume.

8137.title: Metagaming
8137.heading: Metagaming
8137.content:
Metagaming consists of actions, rules, knowledge, or relationships that extend beyond one immediate play session or cross the [[Magic Circle]]. Examples include planning between matches, community norms, or strategic information learned outside the game.

Metagaming can become an outer loop that changes later decisions inside the game. It therefore belongs to the broader [[Game-Player System]] even when it is not encoded directly in the game's internal model.

8140.sourceSearchName: metadata content consistency metadata content consistency
8140.title: Metadata-Content Consistency
8140.heading: Metadata-Content Consistency
8140.content:
Metadata-content consistency tests whether recorded file fields plausibly describe the visible photograph. The stated exposure should agree with motion and focus, a GPS position should fit the depicted place, and the camera or software history should be compatible with the claimed origin.

A contradiction can expose an impossible or incomplete provenance story. Consistency is weaker evidence because metadata can be forged and many combinations of settings can yield similar appearances. The test is best used to generate targeted questions and to corroborate independent forensic cues.

8142.title: MetaCost Relabeling
8142.heading: Document

8143.sourceSearchName: meta cost relabeling meta cost relabeling
8143.title: MetaCost Relabeling
8143.heading: MetaCost Relabeling
8143.content:
MetaCost relabeling converts cost-sensitive classification into an ordinary learning problem by estimating class probabilities and replacing each training label with the class having the lowest expected misclassification cost.

An ensemble supplies more stable probability estimates than a single fitted model. After relabeling, a standard base classifier is trained, allowing cost information to influence algorithms that do not natively support unequal errors.

8144.sourceSearchName: meta cost relabeling meta cost relabeling
8144.title: MetaCost Relabeling
8144.heading: References

8146.title: Metacognition
8146.heading: Metacognition
8146.content:
Metacognition is thinking about one's own thinking. It makes assumptions, habits, and interpretive frames available for inspection rather than leaving them implicit.

For a designer, metacognition supports movement between [[Reductionism]], [[Holism]], and [[Systems Thinking]]. It also helps the designer reason about how a player forms a [[Player Mental Model]] while recognizing the limits of the designer's own perspective.

8148.sourceSearchName: message oriented middleware message oriented middleware
8148.title: Message-Oriented Middleware
8148.heading: Document

8149.sourceSearchName: message oriented middleware message oriented middleware
8149.title: Message-Oriented Middleware
8149.heading: Message-Oriented Middleware
8149.content:
Message-oriented middleware lets applications communicate by placing messages into and retrieving them from a [[Message Queue]]. The queue separates senders from receivers in time and location, so the applications do not have to execute together or use the same internal technology.

The delivery model can specify synchronicity, reliability, transactions, ordering, filtering, addressing, and access control. A shared message model preserves meaning while allowing business logic to remain decoupled.

8150.sourceSearchName: message oriented middleware message oriented middleware
8150.title: Message-Oriented Middleware
8150.heading: References

8152.title: Message Queue
8152.heading: Message Queue
8152.content:
A message queue is a buffer in memory, a database dataset, or a file-backed store where sending applications place messages until receiving applications retrieve them. It allows work to cross application and machine boundaries without requiring both parties to be active at the same instant.

Queues support decoupling, ordering, persistence, filtering, priority, and controlled access. Their delivery behavior must be stated explicitly because reliable, guaranteed, and transacted messages make different promises.

8155.title: Message Priority
8155.heading: Message Priority
8155.content:
Message priority is metadata that allows a receiver or queue to process more urgent messages before ordinary ones. Without an explicit priority rule, a queue commonly retrieves messages in first-in, first-out order.

Priority changes ordering and can delay lower-ranked work during sustained high-priority demand. The levels and starvation behavior should therefore follow a real service requirement rather than being added to every message indiscriminately.

8157.sourceSearchName: message correlation identifier message correlation identifier
8157.title: Message Correlation Identifier
8157.heading: Document

8158.sourceSearchName: message correlation identifier message correlation identifier
8158.title: Message Correlation Identifier
8158.heading: Message Correlation Identifier
8158.content:
A message correlation identifier labels messages that belong to the same task, conversation, sender, or group. A receiver can use it to collect related messages, preserve a sequence within a group, or match a response to the request that caused it.

Correlation lets independent messages retain business context without embedding transport assumptions in application logic. The identifier must remain unique within its intended scope and be propagated across every participating service.

8159.sourceSearchName: message correlation identifier message correlation identifier
8159.title: Message Correlation Identifier
8159.heading: References

8160.sourceSearchName: message authentication code message authentication code
8160.title: Message Authentication Code
8160.heading: Document

8161.sourceSearchName: message authentication code message authentication code
8161.title: Message Authentication Code
8161.heading: Message Authentication Code
8161.content:
A message authentication code is a short keyed value that lets a recipient check both message integrity and possession of the shared authentication key. Altering the message or lacking the key prevents an attacker from producing the expected code.

Unlike an unkeyed [[Cryptographic Hash Function|hash]], the code authenticates a party that holds the key. The source presents it as a lighter form of signature evidence used to support [[Nonrepudiation]].

8162.sourceSearchName: message authentication code message authentication code
8162.title: Message Authentication Code
8162.heading: References

8163.sourceSearchName: mesh rendering component mesh rendering component
8163.title: Mesh Rendering Component
8163.heading: Document

8164.sourceSearchName: mesh rendering component mesh rendering component
8164.title: Mesh Rendering Component
8164.heading: Mesh Rendering Component
8164.content:
A mesh rendering component attaches a three-dimensional mesh and material behavior to a [[Game Actor]]. During drawing it supplies the actor's world transform, binds the required shader and textures, and submits the mesh's vertex array.

Separating mesh rendering from the actor lets the same actor architecture support different visual components. The mesh asset can also be cached and shared while each component retains its own owning actor and draw state.

8165.sourceSearchName: mesh rendering component mesh rendering component
8165.title: Mesh Rendering Component
8165.heading: References

8166.sourceSearchName: mesh normal orientation mesh normal orientation
8166.title: Mesh Normal Orientation
8166.heading: Document

8167.sourceSearchName: mesh normal orientation mesh normal orientation
8167.title: Mesh Normal Orientation
8167.heading: Mesh Normal Orientation
8167.content:
A mesh normal indicates which way a surface faces and influences lighting, shading, and visibility. Face index order helps determine orientation, so reversing that order can flip the normal and make a one-sided exported surface disappear when viewed from the expected side.

Flat shading retains distinct face normals for hard boundaries, while smooth shading blends the normals of adjacent faces to suggest a continuous surface. Normals can even make coarse geometry appear curved, but they do not change the underlying silhouette. Blender tools can flip or recalculate inconsistent normals before export.

8168.sourceSearchName: mesh normal orientation mesh normal orientation
8168.title: Mesh Normal Orientation
8168.heading: References

8170.title: Mesh Network Topology
8170.heading: Mesh Network Topology
8170.content:
A mesh network topology gives nodes an irregular set of point-to-point links, with some nodes connected to several neighbors. A fully connected mesh is the special case in which every node has a direct connection to every other node.

Multiple paths can make a mesh resilient to individual link failures. That resilience requires routing decisions and more connection infrastructure than simpler topologies.

8173.content:
An inset creates a smaller face region inside selected faces and adds the surrounding connecting geometry. It may resemble extruding and scaling inward, but the dedicated operation handles complex selections more consistently.

Inset geometry prepares a surface for later extrusion, deletion, or detail work. Its boundary establishes controlled supporting edges without requiring each new edge to be placed manually.

8176.sourceSearchName: mesh independence study mesh independence study
8176.title: Mesh Independence Study
8176.heading: Mesh Independence Study
8176.content:
A mesh-independence study repeats the same analysis with progressively smaller elements and compares a defined output such as peak temperature, integrated heat flux, or a temperature profile. The selected mesh is adequate when further refinement changes that output insignificantly for the decision.

The comparison must preserve other solver and time-step settings so that spatial discretization is the changing factor. Local refinement near steep gradients can be more efficient than uniform refinement, but it still requires evidence from [[Thermal Mesh Refinement|successive meshes]].

8179.sourceSearchName: mesh extrusion in blender mesh extrusion in blender
8179.title: Mesh Extrusion in Blender
8179.heading: Mesh Extrusion in Blender
8179.content:
Extrusion extends selected mesh components while creating the geometry that connects the old and new positions. It is Blender's central modeling operation because it grows a surface instead of merely moving existing components.

A face extrusion can create a projecting volume, while edges or vertices can extend an open form. After extrusion begins, the new selection can be transformed, constrained, or canceled using the same interaction patterns as other Blender operations.

8182.sourceSearchName: mesh data specification mesh data specification
8182.title: Mesh Data Specification
8182.heading: Mesh Data Specification
8182.content:
A polygon mesh can be specified by vertex coordinates and faces that reference those vertices. Edges may be stated explicitly or derived from face boundaries, while normals describe surface orientation for visibility and lighting. The order of indices in a face can determine which direction its normal points.

This representation separates geometry from the files and applications that carry it. Blender datablocks, OBJ, STL, and PLY make different choices about indexing and supported attributes, but each encodes enough structure to reconstruct a surface. Understanding that shared core makes import, export, and procedural creation easier to reason about.

8183.title: Mesh Data Specification

8185.title: Mesh Component Selection in Blender
8185.heading: Mesh Component Selection in Blender
8185.content:
A mesh is built from vertices, edges, and faces. A vertex is a point, an edge joins two vertices, and a face is a polygon bounded by at least three connected edges.

Edit mode can select any of these component types. Wireframe or X-ray display makes components on the far side selectable, while ordinary solid display limits selection to visible geometry and helps avoid unintended changes through the model.

8188.title: Mesh Beveling in Blender
8188.heading: Mesh Beveling in Blender
8188.content:
Beveling replaces a sharp mesh corner with additional geometry that forms a rounded or flattened transition. Even objects perceived as sharp usually have a small edge radius, so bevels help a model respond to light more plausibly.

The Bevel tool works on selected components and can vary the width and segmentation of the transition. It adds detail where a perfectly mathematical corner would look unnaturally harsh.

8191.title: Mesh and Time-Step Coupling
8191.heading: Mesh and Time-Step Coupling
8191.content:
Spatial element size and temporal step size jointly control a transient finite-element solution. A fine mesh cannot recover a rapid event skipped by coarse time steps, while very small time steps cannot resolve a steep spatial gradient on an inadequate mesh.

Both settings affect cost and convergence, and adaptive solvers may vary the actual step during a run. Separate [[Mesh Independence Study|mesh]] and [[Time-Step Independence Study|time-step]] checks help identify which discretization limits the accuracy of a reported peak or history.
